Subject: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity SLOs & sizing (FinTechCo)

Hi Sara / Tom — thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps related to dedicated capacity performance validation: 

Call recap (from our side):
- Primary SLO: 95th p95 latency <= 200ms for single-turn generation (chat) at typical prompt lengths (avg ~120 tokens).
- Peak concurrency target: 200 concurrent sessions; typical sustained concurrency 80–120.
- Throughput objective: sustained 50 requests/sec (50rps) with bursts to 120rps for short periods.
- Streaming: client expects partial token streaming (flush every ~50ms) for UX; important for latency-sensitive flows.
- Quality: want to test with your production prompt set (you mentioned the payment reconciliation assistant).

Proposed internal next steps:
1) We’ll validate sizing for Dedicated (GPU SKU comparisons: A10 vs A100 vs H100 alternatives), provide reserved throughput per pool and suggested shard counts.
2) Provide a draft performance validation plan (bench commands, sample payloads, target metrics).
3) Share a sizing matrix and benchmark artifacts.

Action items for FinTechCo:
- Please share a representative workload sample (anonymized prompts / token distribution) and any max request/response token limits.
- Confirm the latency SLO and whether p95 or p99 is the gating metric.
- Any hard limits for cold-starts / auth latency we should account for?

I’ll kick this over to Marissa and Aditya to assemble the sizing and baseline benchmarks; Rafael will run GPU-level profiling. We’ll aim to have a recommended Dedicated configuration and test plan by end of day Thursday (2027-07-08).

Attachments: draft-sizing-matrix (coming), initial benchmark notes (coming).

Thanks —
Alex Martinez
Enterprise Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks Alex — this looks good. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Confirmed SLO: p95 latency <= 200ms is our primary gating metric. p99 is nice-to-have but not blocking for initial rollout.
- Token distribution: attached is an anonymized sample (fintech-workload-sample.jsonl) with prompt/response token counts; avg request 120 tokens, avg response 160 tokens.
- Concurrency: 200 concurrent clients is our peak expected during end-of-month batch support windows; normally 80–100 concurrent.
- Streaming behavior: yes, streaming partial responses is required for the customer UX — ideally flushes every 50–100ms depending on network.
- Cold-start: our clients are long-lived; cold-starts should be rare, but warmup on pool scale-up should not exceed 2s for first token.

I’m attaching the workload sample and a short doc with our UX streaming expectations. Let us know if you need any more telemetry from our side.

Best,

Quick sizing pass attached (dedicated-sizing-matrix.xlsx) — highlights below: 

High-level recommendation (initial):
- A100 (40GB) reserved pools: 4 GPUs per pool => estimated sustained throughput ~55–65 rps (single-turn, 8k model), p95 ~140–180ms depending on batching policy. Handles KV cache for 8k context with room for aggressive batching.
- A10 (24GB) reserved pools: 6 GPUs per pool => estimated sustained throughput ~30–40 rps, p95 ~220–300ms under similar batching; could meet cost targets but may miss p95 target at peak without higher shard counts.
- H100: best headroom and scaling for larger context / p99, but cost + availability trade-offs; recommended if FinTechCo requires heavy multimodal or 16k contexts.

Suggested config: start with A100 pool (4x), reserved throughput configured to 60rps with autoscale burst to 120rps for short durations; set continuous batching window to 20ms target and enable token-level flush for streaming.

Attachments: dedicated-sizing-matrix.xlsx (contains per-GPU rps estimates, shard counts, and cost delta). I’ll iterate once Rafael uploads benchmark PDF.

—Marissa
Staff Product Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Jul 2027 11:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity SLOs & sizing (FinTechCo)

Rafael and I ran a quick A10 vs A100 benchmark against the sample payload this morning; Rafael will attach the PDF with detailed numbers (gpu-benchmark-results.pdf). Key runtime notes: 
- Enable continuous batching with max_batch_delay=20ms and target batch_size based on empirical client arrival (we saw best p95 at batch sizes ~4–8 for this workload).
- Use per-request token flush (token_flush_interval_ms=50) for streaming; we measured steady client-side perceived latency improvements.
- KV cache: for 8k context we prefer per-GPU KV to avoid cross-GPU transfer during generation; this increases memory pressure but reduces tail latency.
- Reserved throughput settings: set per-GPU reserved_rps to 15 for A100 (4 GPU pool => 60rps), for A10 set reserved_rps to 5 (6 GPU pool => 30rps).

Next: Rafael to upload the benchmark PDF; Marissa to finalize sizing matrix; Alex to send recommended config to FinTechCo and propose a short validation window (48–72 hours) for acceptance testing.

Thanks,
Aditya
Senior Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference
